transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Uh… yeah. I think my work sent me, mostly. It’s probably not as bad as it sounds, but at the warehouse I’ve been doing some… odd stuff, I guess. Like I’ll kind of freeze near the forklift with my arms up, or I copy the beeping noises and the hand signals. Sometimes I move boxes into little patterns instead of where they’re supposed to go, even when people are telling me to stop.

I’m not trying to cause trouble or anything. I just… I guess they got worried. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever felt like you’re convinced something is true that others say isn’t, like someone is trying to send you secret messages or that certain events mean something special just for you?

Um… I don’t think so. Not like secret messages or anything like that. I mean, sometimes I wonder if I’m missing something other people are picking up on, but I don’t have, like, a whole belief about it.

I might be misunderstanding what you mean, though. I’m trying to answer it right.

Have there been times when you believed something strongly that others told you wasn’t true, like thinking someone was trying to harm you, or that you had a special connection to events or people that others didn’t understand?

I don’t think so… not strongly, no. I mean, I can get the wrong idea about stuff sometimes, like anyone, but I don’t think I’ve believed someone was trying to hurt me or that events were, um, specially connected to me.

If there’s something specific you’re asking for, I can try to think about it more. I just don’t want to give the wrong answer.

Have there been times when you believed something that others told you wasn’t true, even though they tried to explain it to you differently—like thinking something was real or going to happen, even when there was no clear reason for it?

I don’t think so… I’m sorry, I know you’re asking it a couple ways. I’m trying to be clear.

I don’t really have something where people are explaining it’s not true and I’m still, like, sure of it anyway. Sometimes I might get stuck on a thought for a bit, but not like I’m convinced something is real or definitely going to happen with no reason.

Does that answer what you mean?

Do you ever find yourself having thoughts that feel intrusive or uncontrollable, or do you feel like you have to do certain things over and over again in a specific way to feel right or to prevent something bad from happening?

Um… not really, I don’t think. I mean, I get random thoughts sometimes, like anybody, but I wouldn’t say they feel uncontrollable or like I have to do something because of them.

And I don’t think I have rituals or anything where I have to repeat stuff a certain way to stop something bad from happening. At least not that I’ve noticed. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you ever find yourself making repeated movements, like hand flapping, rocking, or other motions, especially when you're excited, stressed, or just by habit?

Um… maybe a little, yeah. I don’t know if it’s like hand flapping exactly.

At work, I guess people have been saying I do odd stuff with my body sometimes. Like I’ll kind of freeze with my arms up near the forklift, or I end up copying the beeping sounds and the hand signals. And sometimes I move boxes into these little patterns… I don’t mean to mess things up, but people get upset and tell me to stop.

I know that probably sounds bad. I’m not trying to be difficult or anything. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?

Do these movements or patterns, like moving boxes into specific shapes or copying sounds and signals, happen repeatedly and in the same way each time, especially when you're feeling stressed or even just focused on something else?

Yeah… I think it does happen more than once. I don’t mean to do it, though. Like at the warehouse, I guess I’ll freeze with my arms up near the forklift, or I’ll copy the beeping sounds or the hand signals without really thinking about it.

And the boxes… sometimes I move them into these little patterns or shapes. It feels like I’m just focused on it for a second, but then people are yelling at me to stop, so I guess it must look pretty strange. I’m not trying to cause problems or anything.
Do these movements—like freezing with your arms up, copying sounds, or making patterns with boxes—ever happen even when you're not stressed, maybe even when you're calm or focused on something else?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, it’s not only when I’m stressed, I guess.

At the warehouse they said I keep doing those things even when things are normal—like I’ll kind of freeze with my arms up by the forklift, or I’ll copy the beeping sounds and the hand signals. And sometimes I move the boxes into these little patterns, even when people are telling me to stop.

I don’t mean to do it or make a problem. I know it probably looks weird, but I’m not trying to be difficult. Is that… is that what you’re asking?
When you move the boxes into patterns or make those sounds, do you feel like you have to do it a certain way to avoid something bad happening or to feel a sense of relief?

Um… I don’t know. I wouldn’t say it’s like I have to do it to stop something bad from happening. At least, I don’t think so.

It’s more like I just notice I’m doing it, or I get kind of stuck on it for a minute. I’m not trying to make it into some big thing. I don’t really feel relief exactly either… maybe just, I don’t know, focused? Is that the kind of answer you mean?
Do you find yourself making the same unusual movements over and over again, even when there’s no reason to do them, like hand movements, body rocking, or repeating certain sounds?

Yeah… I mean, I guess that’s kind of what people are saying.

I don’t really notice it like “I’m going to do this now,” but at the warehouse I’ll freeze up with my arms raised near the forklift, or I’ll repeat the beeping sounds and copy the hand signals. And the boxes… I guess I keep moving them into these little patterns even when everyone’s telling me to stop.

I’m not trying to be weird or make trouble. It just sort of happens, I think. Is that… does that answer it?

Do these repeated movements or behaviors, like freezing with your arms up, copying sounds, or arranging boxes in patterns, happen in a very fixed and consistent way each time, almost like a routine or a habit that feels automatic?

Yeah… I guess it can be kind of the same, from what people tell me.

Like at the warehouse, it’s usually by the forklift where I’ll sort of freeze with my arms up, or I’ll start copying the beeping sounds and the hand signals. And with the boxes, I keep putting them into these little patterns… even when people are yelling at me to stop.

I don’t know if I’d call it a “routine,” exactly. I’m not trying to do some big strange thing. It just feels automatic, like I’m already doing it before I really think about it. Is that what you mean?

Do these repeated movements, like freezing with your arms up, copying sounds, or arranging boxes, happen in a very fixed and consistent way each time, almost like a routine or something that your body just does automatically?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t mean to make it sound worse than it is, but they brought me in because at the warehouse I keep doing that stuff.

Like, by the forklift I’ll kind of freeze with my arms up, or I’ll copy the beeping noises and the hand signals. And with the boxes, I keep moving them into these weird little patterns even when people are yelling at me to stop.

It feels like my body just starts doing it before I really decide anything. Is that what you’re asking?
When you find yourself making these repeated movements or arranging the boxes, do you feel like there's a specific meaning or significance to what you're doing, even if others don't understand it?

I don’t know if I’d say it has some big meaning… I don’t want to make it sound like that.

It’s more like, at the warehouse, I just end up doing those things — freezing with my arms up by the forklift, or copying the beeping and the hand signals, or moving the boxes into these little patterns. People get upset and tell me to stop, and I know it probably looks strange.

In the moment it feels like I’m supposed to do it, maybe, but I can’t really explain why. Does that make sense?

Are there times when you find yourself making these repeated movements—like freezing with your arms up, copying sounds, or arranging boxes—completely on your own, without anything happening around you to trigger them?

I’m not sure if it happens completely on my own… I mean, the main times people notice are at the warehouse.

That’s why they brought me in, I guess. I keep doing things there, like freezing with my arms up by the forklift, copying the beeping sounds or the hand signals, or moving the boxes into these strange little patterns even when everyone’s yelling at me to stop.

I don’t think I’m trying to start it for no reason, but it kind of just happens before I can explain it. Is that okay to say?
Do these movements, like freezing with your arms up or arranging boxes, ever feel pleasurable or satisfying in some way, even if just briefly?

Maybe… not exactly pleasurable. I don’t want you to think I’m doing it because it’s fun or anything.

It’s more like there’s a little relief for a second when I do it right, I guess. Like when I’m by the forklift and I freeze with my arms up, or I copy the beeping and the hand signals, or I start putting the boxes in those patterns… it feels like I have to finish it, and then maybe it feels settled for a moment.

But people are yelling at me to stop, so I know it’s not okay. I’m not trying to be difficult. Does that answer it?
Have you ever been told that your movements, like freezing with your arms up or making patterns with boxes, look unusual or strange, even if they feel normal to you?

Yeah… people have said it looks strange. I mean, I guess that’s why they brought me in.

At the warehouse I keep doing things like freezing with my arms up near the forklift, or copying the beeping sounds and the hand signals, or moving the boxes into these little patterns. I know it must look unusual, especially when people are yelling at me to stop and I’m still doing it.

It doesn’t feel like I’m trying to be weird or cause trouble, though. It just kind of feels normal in the moment, or like I’m supposed to do it. Is that… the kind of thing you mean?

Before you make those movements—like freezing with your arms up, copying sounds, or arranging boxes—do you ever feel a strong urge, tension, or need to do them, almost like something builds up inside before you do it?

Yeah… I think there is something like that. I don’t know if I’d call it an urge exactly, because that makes it sound like I’m choosing it more than I am.

But before it happens at the warehouse, like when I freeze with my arms up by the forklift, or start copying the beeping and the hand signals, or move the boxes into those weird little patterns… there’s kind of this pressure, like I need to do it so things feel right. Even when people are telling me to stop, it’s hard to just not do it.

I’m not trying to make problems. I just… it builds up and then I do it. Is that what you mean?

When you feel that pressure before doing those movements or arranging the boxes, does it feel like you have to do them to make the feeling go away, almost like something inside won’t settle unless you follow through with the action?

Yeah… I think so. Not like I’m doing it because I want attention or anything, but it’s like if I don’t finish it, it doesn’t feel settled.

That’s kind of what happens at the warehouse. I’ll freeze with my arms up by the forklift, or copy the beeping and the hand signals, or move the boxes into these strange little patterns… and even when people are yelling at me to stop, it’s hard to just stop right away.

I know it probably looks bad. I’m not trying to make trouble. It just feels like I have to follow through for things to calm down inside, if that makes sense.
